summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and multiple airway reconstructions was admitted due to persistent green sputum and subjective chills following a recent hospitalization where Pseudomonas aeruginosa was identified. She remained on oral ciprofloxacin but reported no improvement in sputum color or chest and throat pain. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, clear lungs on imaging, and no signs of acute infection on fiberoptic exam. Sputum gram stain showed inflammation but no bacterial growth, suggesting resolved infection with ongoing chronic mucus production. She was managed conservatively, continued on ciprofloxacin to complete her course, and evaluated by the pain team for chronic pain management. She remained stable, maintained oxygenation, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and interventional pulmonology.
